problems: Both dossiers validate with --resolve (0 errors, 0 warnings); all ten findings applied. norman-england, kingdom-of-the-isles and kingdom-of-powys-wenwynwyn were not touched.

Auvergne: the reviewer's alternative (Treaty of Louviers) is not on any opened page (Louviers, Richard I and Angevin Empire pages are silent or undated); the Philip II page dates Henry II's renunciation of suzerainty over Auvergne to July 1189, so the loss stays in 1189 at confidence 2 with that source.

Gascony: the Angevin dossier now hands the Gascon core to duchy-of-aquitaine in 1204 (keyframes 1204, 1205, 1206 without it). kingdom-of-england /ledger/34 (1210 gain from angevin-empire) uses Cliopatria's 1210 England shape, which holds the same 861 cells as the 1206 Angevin shape, Gascony included, so England and duchy-of-aquitaine would draw Gascony twice from 1210 unless one gives it up.

Anglo-Norman Ireland is drawn twice: lordship-of-ireland (with kingdom-of-leinster, kingdom-of-meath, kingdom-of-desmond, kingdom-of-thomond, ulaid, kingdom-of-connacht now written) and the Angevin Empire (Leinster and Waterford 1171, Ulaid and Munster 1177, Cliopatria cells to 1209). The Angevin counterpart strings (Kingdom of Leinster, Kingdom of Ulaid, Kingdom of Desmond and Thomond, Ruaidri Ua Conchobair) were left as written; the orchestrator should choose one owner or make the lordship a vassal of the empire.

Norman Vexin: this ledger follows the capture (1193, Richard I and Philip II pages) and treats Le Goulet (1200) as confirmation; kingdom-of-france, royal-domain-of-france and the Crown lands page date the Vexin gain to 1200 and royal-domain-of-france dates Berry to May 1200 (here 1199, Angevin Empire page).

duchy-of-brittany has no mirror for the Angevin protectorate tint 1181-1206 (it has the occupation 1166-1181, Nantes 1158/1185 and the 1164 lands, which now match); delete the two Angevin vassal events if eu-10 does not want it. county-of-poitou (1205) and duchy-of-aquitaine (1204) now mirror Angevin losses.

Missing mirrors elsewhere: kingdom-of-powys (1169 loss of the Corwen cell to Fadog), kingdom-of-powys-wenwynwyn (1210 loss of the Llansilin cell to Fadog), kingdom-of-gwynedd (vassal relation of Fadog 1258-1277; its /ledger/32-33 name angevin-empire for Tegeingl, which no Angevin shape holds), kingdom-of-england (Fadog 1277 and 1284 vassal events, Norman Vexin), kingdom-of-france (Auvergne 1189, Vexin 1160 and 1193).
